summary:
The scanner now counts out of LastAccessKept, once, each kept folder at or under the Windows folder that has a child folder whose own keep-open succeeded. The Windows folder is held as LongPath.NormalizeRoot(GetFolderPath(Windows)).Win32 and compared with the existing IsAtOrUnder. The rule is keyed on a successful child keep-open, not an attempted one. ScanResult.LastAccessKept's contract is now worded as that rule, with its known gaps.

On the test side: TempTree moves its trees out of a TEMP inside the Windows folder, and refuses by name when the redirect target is inside it too. HeldOpenTreeTests and LastAccessTests now back-date deepest first. New default-suite tests (LastAccessUnderSystemRootTests) build in C:\Windows\Temp\fsa-tests on purpose and assert kept == folders still old. TempTreeRootTests covers the root choice. The two SL-096 fitness rules are closed as classes, each through a JSON corpus fed by LastAccessRuleCorpusTests, plus a reflection check for what no line pattern can see. The triage record is docs/design/SL-096-last-access-under-windows-temp.md.

Results:
- The SL-096 bug project exits 0.
- The full suite is 789/789 with exit 0 under TEMP=C:\WINDOWS\TEMP (both with the shell's TEMP set and with `dotnet test -e`) and under the user's own TEMP.
- The Facts report kept 4 of 7 with root, plain and links moved, for all three root spellings, and kept 1 of 2 for the refusing child (truth 1).
- With the correction taken out, they fail with kept 7 against 4.

What was already in the tree: the engine-appended fitness.yaml block was rewritten as the M1/m2 fixes. The untracked bug project is kept unchanged as the acceptance test. .taad-scratch/ was left untouched.

files.why: CountListingOpen(asked, folderPath) counts a kept parent under the Windows folder out once when a child folder's keep-open succeeds. WindowsFolderFromEnvironment normalises %SystemRoot% to \\?\ form, and returns null when the environment names none (review m1). Both callers (ListRoot and the walk) pass the path. Class remarks state the limit.

LastAccessKept doc comment rewritten as the rule (review m3). Says nothing is read back. Lists the known gaps: within-the-hour or updates off, a -1 set that fails after a successful open, ProgramData/ProgramFiles unmeasured, spelling-matched root, and the root's parent.

Pure internal ChooseTestsRoot(tempPath, windowsDir, localAppData) redirects out of the Windows folder and refuses a target that is under it too. New internal TempTree(string testsRoot) constructor. The NTFS check reads the chosen root. Outside() builds beside the tree's own root.
Back-dates deepest first, spike 2's line: Enumerable.Reverse(Observed), then c.txt, then control.
Back-dates open and refusing\sub before Root (spike 2's line).

Default-suite tests in C:\Windows\Temp\fsa-tests: the nested tree as a Theory over the root's spelling (as-is, lower-case, trailing-separator), the refusing child, and the same nested tree outside the Windows folder. Each asserts kept == folders still old and that the tree is gone after Dispose.

ChooseTestsRoot branches: redirect in any letter case, prefix-only names left alone, a system/service-profile target refused by name, no Windows folder named, and this run's trees outside the Windows folder.

Feeds both corpora to the rules read from .taad/fitness.yaml (and to CountingRuleTestsAreNeverSkipped's patterns). TheWindowsFolderFactsRunInTheDefaultSuite checks by reflection: the class is public, each test carries one stock Fact or Theory and nothing else, nothing sets Skip, and the default filter has no by-name clause.
O-016 corpus: 21 fire, 10 quiet and 3 known-miss routes into %SystemRoot%\Temp, each with what the design's patterns did.
O-018 corpus: 27 fire, 10 quiet and 4 reflection-closed ways to take the Windows-folder Facts out of the default run.
SettledPatterns made internal so the new corpus test reuses the one yaml reader rather than copying it.
Comment at SyncRootRig's GetTempPath naming the rule exemption and the filed slice that removes it (M1's fix).

The two SL-096 settled rules the engine appended, rewritten. Rule 1 per m2: any Trait, custom *Fact/*Theory attributes, FactAttribute/TheoryAttribute subclasses, and Skip-family properties. Rule 2 per M1: Path.GetTempPath/GetTempFileName, CreateTempSubdirectory, the TEMP/TMP/SystemRoot/windir variables, and broader literal spellings, with except_files for FailCriticalErrorsTests.cs and CloudPlaceholderTests.cs. Names put on one line and patterns single-quoted so the shared reader can parse them.
Triage record: the verdict for each test, the mechanism, what was ruled out, what changed, what this build measured, and the limits.

obligations.how: Ran the acceptance command after the fix: 'Passed! - Failed: 0, Passed: 1', exit 0. The bug project is unchanged and kept out of FsAnalyser.slnx. Validate owns the final run.

LastAccessUnderSystemRootTests.AScanUnderTheWindowsTempFolderCountsAsKeptOnlyTheFoldersThatStayedOld builds the 7-folder, 4-file tree in C:\Windows\Temp\fsa-tests, back-dates it deepest first, scans it and asserts asked 7 and kept == still old. Measured: kept 4 of 7, moved root, plain and links.

LastAccessUnderSystemRootTests.AChildThatRefusesWriteAttributesLeavesItsParentCountedAsKept: R\refusing\x.bin with a deny FILE_WRITE_ATTRIBUTES ACE on refusing, back-dated x.bin then R. Measured: kept 1 of 2, 1 still old, nothing moved.
The lower-case row of the Theory scans c:\windows\temp\fsa-tests\<guid>. Measured: kept 4 of 7, 4 still old.
The trailing-separator row of the Theory scans the root plus a backslash, labelled a redundant spelling check per m5. Measured: kept 4 of 7, 4 still old.

LastAccessUnderSystemRootTests.OutsideTheWindowsFolderEveryKeptFolderStaysKept: same tree under TempTree's default root, which is asserted to be outside the Windows folder. Measured: (asked, kept, still old) = (7, 7, 7). LastAccessTests (4,3) and HeldOpenTreeTests (8,8) still pass under both TEMPs.

Full suite with TEMP=TMP=C:\WINDOWS\TEMP: 789 passed, 0 failed, exit 0. Run once with the shell's env and once through `dotnet test -e TEMP=C:\WINDOWS\TEMP -e TMP=C:\WINDOWS\TEMP` from a shell whose TEMP was the user's.

Full suite with the user's TEMP (C:\Users\sshub\AppData\Local\Temp): 789/789, exit 0. Run with the shell's env and with `-e`. The -e form was shown to reach the test host: a bogus Q:\ TEMP crashed it.
TempTreeRootTests.ATempAtOrUnderTheWindowsFolderIsReplacedByTheUsersOwn: C:\WINDOWS\TEMP\, c:\windows\temp, C:\Windows\Temp\deeper\ and C:\Windows\ all give C:\Users\u\AppData\Local\Temp\fsa-tests.

TempTreeRootTests.ATempThatOnlySharesTheWindowsFoldersNameIsUsedAsItIs: C:\WindowsTemp\, C:\Windows.old\Temp\ and C:\Windows2\Temp each stay <temp>\fsa-tests. The comparison is Scanner.IsAtOrUnder at a separator.

TempTreeRootTests.ARedirectTargetThatIsNotOutsideTheWindowsFolderIsRefusedByName: systemprofile, a lower-case ServiceProfiles path and an empty LOCALAPPDATA each throw InvalidOperationException. The message names TEMP, the Windows folder, 'system or service profile' and the remedy.

Every LastAccessUnderSystemRootTests case runs through InTree, which disposes the tree and asserts the \\?\ root no longer exists. The refusing-child case holds the deny ACE, and Dispose clears it before Directory.Delete. After all runs, C:\Windows\Temp\fsa-tests lists 0 entries.

The nested-tree Theory is the standing check. With `_lastAccessKept--` made a no-op (Scanner.cs rewritten, so it rebuilds), all three rows fail: '(asked, kept) = (7, 7), but 4 of the 7 folders ... Kept over-counts'.

Measured by AChildThatRefusesWriteAttributesLeavesItsParentCountedAsKept under C:\WINDOWS\Temp\fsa-tests: 'kept 1 of 2; 1 of 2 folders still at least 47 h old; moved: none'. The successful-keep-open rule matches the truth (1). Owed to validate, which can re-run that filter.

Not measurable here: no Windows 10 machine exists (Q-205), and writing test folders under %ProgramData% or %ProgramFiles% is the person's step. The triage doc and the ScanResult contract record both as unmeasured and uncorrected.

Rule 2 now bans every .NET route to the process temp folder (Path.GetTempPath/GetTempFileName, Directory.CreateTempSubdirectory, the TEMP/TMP variables read or expanded) and the Windows folder's Temp in any drive letter, case, separator, `+`/`,` form and environment variable. except_files: FailCriticalErrorsTests.cs and CloudPlaceholderTests.cs, which carries a comment naming the filed slice. Corpus of 34 rows; 13 rows read before=quiet/now=fire. The test asserts the design's 3 patterns stay quiet on them, which shows the before-fix code failing those rows. Emulating the rule over every Core.Tests file, comments included, hits only excepted files.

Scanner.WindowsFolderFromEnvironment holds %SystemRoot% as LongPath.NormalizeRoot(GetFolderPath(Windows)).Win32, computed once per Run. It returns null, so nothing is corrected, when the folder is empty, whitespace or not fully qualified. With the bare GetFolderPath value instead, the Theory fails 3 of 3.

ScanResult.LastAccessKept is now worded as the rule: asked folders whose keep-open succeeded, minus each such folder at or under %SystemRoot% with a child folder whose keep-open succeeded. It says this was measured to move the parent on this machine and that nothing reads a time back. Both divergences are recorded as known gaps, with no flag added. The triage doc says the same.

obligations.how: No scratch-copy procedure is owed. The regression check is the committed Theory itself, and this build measured it red with the correction removed (kept 7 vs 4, 3 of 3 rows), restoring the file afterwards. The spike 1 tree (d) outcome is pinned by the refusing-child Fact's equality.

The trailing-separator row is kept and its doc comment labels it redundant: Scan trims the separator before anything compares, so it is a spelling check, not a material case. The lower-case row rests on the case-insensitive IsAtOrUnder comparison.
obligations.not_mutable: A labelling change: the row passes with or without any fix, because Scan's NormalizeRoot trims the separator first. That is the point of m5.

deviations: Rule 1's Trait clause is `\bTrait(Attribute)?\s*\(`, not the critique's `\[\s*Trait\s*\(`. The critique's form misses `[Fact, Trait("Network", ...)]`, which the design's own pattern caught (corpus S18/S19), and `[TraitAttribute(...)]` (S27). The custom-attribute pattern starts at `[` or `,` rather than `[` alone, to catch `[Fact, WindowsTempFact]` (S23). `Skip\s*=` became `\bSkip\w*\s*=`, to catch xUnit v3's SkipWhen/SkipUnless on data rows (S05).

The optional `:\s*(FactAttribute|TheoryAttribute)\b` went into SL-096's settled rule 1, not into the twinned CountingRuleTestsAreNeverSkipped. Changing a twinned rule would move the parity counts that RuleCases and SettledCountProbe pin literally (Q-085).

Rule 2 bans more than M1's single `Path\.GetTempPath\s*\(`, because the obligation says close the class. It also bans GetTempFileName, Directory.CreateTempSubdirectory, GetEnvironmentVariable/ExpandEnvironmentVariables of TEMP/TMP/SystemRoot/windir, other drive letters, forward slashes, a lower-case "temp" and `+` concatenation. Each is a corpus row.

Added LastAccessRuleCorpusTests.TheWindowsFolderFactsRunInTheDefaultSuite, a reflection check that the design did not name. It closes the members of m2's class that no line pattern can see: a non-public class, a deleted [Fact], a foreign attribute, a by-name clause in the default filter.

TempTree's root is no longer a static field. It is chosen on each construction and kept in an instance field, so a refusal is a named InvalidOperationException rather than a TypeInitializationException that poisons every test. As a consequence Outside() now builds beside the tree's own root. That is what waived O-023 (m7, carried as SC-174) asked for; it fell out of the structure rather than being built on purpose.

The engine-appended SL-096 yaml entries were reformatted: each name on one line and patterns single-quoted, with the same YAML values. This lets the existing SettledPatterns reader, made internal, feed them to the corpus tests. The `because` texts were updated for M1/m2.
LastAccessRuleCorpusTests builds the route rule's name from two string pieces, so the file does not spell `%SystemRoot%\Temp` and need its own exemption from the rule it tests.

The cases for the whole suite under each TEMP (C-006, C-007) use `dotnet test -e TEMP=... -e TMP=...` rather than the design's `$env:TEMP=...;` form, which is shell syntax the engine's commands cannot carry. -e was shown to reach the test host: a bogus TEMP crashed it. C-007's path is this machine's own %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp, written out.
not_built: The engine launching test runs with the HKCU TEMP/TMP (spike 5): taad_v3's launch.py is outside this repository.
Routing SyncRootRig/CloudRig (opt-in Cloud=CF-SYNC-ROOT) through TempTree's root choice: filed by the design. CloudPlaceholderTests.cs is exempt from rule 2 by name until then.
Any change that avoids the parent's last-access move (plain-open children, holding parent handles): Q-207 decided against it, and Q-159 defers it.
Widening the correction to %ProgramData%/%ProgramFiles%: unmeasured, and writing there is the person's step.
A KnownWorkarounds entry or an in-app notice: no app behaviour steps around luafv. The scan does what it did, the correction fixes this project's own count, and the redirect lives in test fixtures.
Keying the per-scan set by store entry index (m6, waived and carried as SC-173): the design's path-text set is built.
A GetFinalPathNameByHandleW comparison for roots reaching the Windows folder by another spelling (m9, waived and carried as SC-176): recorded as a limit only.

Removing the survey's leftover C:\Windows\Temp\fsa-sl096survey-<8 hex> folder: its name cannot be listed by this user, and the admin operations on offer (whoami, read-denied-folders, which returns counts and never names) cannot find it.
follow_ups: Engine mutation runner: restoring a mutated file with Copy-Item kept its older timestamp, and MSBuild then skipped the rebuild. The DLL kept the mutated code and the next test run failed spuriously (seen in this build: the bug test went red until Scanner.cs was touched). When the engine puts a mutated file back, it should touch it or force a rebuild.
taad_v3 launch.py: give test runs the user's HKCU TEMP/TMP (spike 5 measured 23/23 with it).
Slice: route SyncRootRig/CloudRig through TempTree.ChooseTestsRoot and drop CloudPlaceholderTests.cs from rule 2's except_files.
Person (admin): confirm luafv.sys is the driver (fltmc, or a trace), and remove the survey's leftover folder in C:\Windows\Temp.
Person: measure whether a write-class child open moves the parent in %ProgramData% and %ProgramFiles%. If it does, widen WindowsFolderFromEnvironment's location list.
Person: run LastAccessUnderSystemRootTests and the 23 last-access tests on Windows 10 (Q-205).
SC-174 (m7) can likely close: TempTree.Outside() now builds under the root the tree was given.

.taad-scratch/ (investigation probes, run logs, and small trees under .taad-scratch/temp/fsa-tests) is untracked in this worktree and was left untouched. Someone should decide whether it is committed or discarded.
